dedupe_keys.name: infrasound array dataset of the 2021 eruptive paroxysms of etna volcano

description: Infrasound Array Dataset of the 2021 Eruptive Paroxysms of Etna Volcano is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Luciano Zuccarello et al. Infrasound is a valuable tool for volcano monitoring that can offer critical insights into volcanic processes, unrest and eruption. Over the last two decades, studies have shown the benefits of using local infrasound arrays - clusters of sensors near active vents - for real-time detection, tracking, and quantifying eruption intensity. Coverage: not stated; published in 2026. Formats: Image. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 9994042666 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
